items.title: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 21 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding five receptions for 47 yards.
items.text: Gibbs is the most valuable player in fantasy football, regardless of format. Since scoring twice from one yard out isn’t enough for him, Gibbs ripped off a clean 70-yard touchdown run on the Lions’ ninth drive — and that probably wasn’t his most impressive play. One drive earlier, Gibbs took a run to the right side, and multiple Bears defenders broke past the offensive line. One got a hand on him, but he changed direction and took off for a 32-yard gain down the sideline. The impending 2026 league-winner should be treated as the overall RB1 in Week 13 against the Falcons’ beatable run defense.

items.title: Sam LaPorta caught 4-of-5 targets for 44 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears.
items.text: The Lions’ No. 1 tight end generated multiple double-digit gains today, including an 11-yard touchdown on a hitch-and-go just before halftime. He played through his ankle injury without issue after beginning the week limited in practice, notably diving to make a 17-yard catch. LaPorta is a TE1 against the Falcons next week. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Jameson Williams caught 6-of-9 targets for 68 yards in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding one rush for 12 yards.
items.text: The Lions got Williams involved on crossers, corners and screen passes today, but a few missed connections proved costly. Jared Goff targeted Williams in the end zone on the opening drive, but the pass fell incomplete. On the Lions’ fifth drive, Williams got behind the defense, but stumbled slightly, resulting in an overthrow instead of a long score. On the Lions’ 10th drive, Williams was unable to secure a third-down target at the Bears’ 25-yard line and accidentally tipped the pass to a Bears safety instead. That said, Williams deserves credit for generating a 39-yard gain on a corner route

items.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 7-of-10 targets for 146 yards in the Lions’ Week 12 loss to the Bears.
items.text: St. Brown shot out of the gates in this one, generating two explosive plays on the Lions’ opening drive. He needed a breather after being sandwiched between two Bears defenders on a deep completion on the Lions’ third drive. He played through a ribs issue a couple of weeks ago, and may reappear on the injury report with the same issue next week. Despite the hard hit, St. Brown stayed hot and continued ripping off long gains. A Bears defensive back committed pass interference against him on a target thrown to St. Brown right at the goal line. The ball fell incomplete, but the penalty setup one

items.title: Dallas Goedert (shoulder) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Cowboys.
items.text: Goedert suffered a shoulder injury on the first drive of the game and was ruled out a quarter later. The 31-year-old will get a week-plus to get healthy for Week 13 against the Cardinals, but for now Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt will be the uninspiring tight end options. - Christopher Crawford

items.title: Jared Goff completed 25-of-36 passes for 313 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Lions’ 35-39, Week 12 loss to the Bears, adding three rushes for 10 yards.
items.text: Goff’s first career Thanksgiving interception was not his fault. Jameson Williams tipped the pass right into Bears S Dillon Thieneman’s hands. Goff played very well on the day, and looked unstoppable whenever he targeted Amon-Ra St. Brown. Goff nearly tacked on a second passing touchdown on a trick-play pass to OL Larry Borom in the end zone, but the pass unfortunately fell incomplete. Goff remains a locked-in QB1 next week against the Falcons. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Salvon Ahmed rushed three times for 50 yards in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding two receptions for 17 yards.
items.text: Ahmed provided the Bears with needed sparks on more than one occasion today, using his speed to initially rip off a 46-yard run on the Bears’ third drive. He later made a slick diving catch for a first down on the Bears’ 10th drive. He can be picked up in 14-team leagues at this time, though he is only a bench stash. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Kyle Monangai rushed eight times for 15 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding one reception for 14 yards.
items.text: Monangai ran inefficiently this week, but that did not stop him from bullying his way into the end zone for a pair of short touchdowns. The burly back may still be rounding into form after his lengthy turf toe-related absence, but he remains a featured player in the Bears’ elite offense. Monangai is an RB2/FLEX against the Jaguars next week. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: D’Andre Swift rushed nine times for 65 yards and one touchdown in the Bears’ Week 12 win over the Lions, adding seven receptions for 97 yards.
items.text: Swift was extremely efficient on his touches against the Lions, which was good because the Bears got Kyle Monangai and Salvon Ahmed going in this one as well. Swift had two 30-plus-yard gains today. His first was a catch in the flats, which he took down the right sideline after juking two Lions defenders. The second was a clean touchdown run in which he faked right before cutting back to the left and outrunning the defense. He regularly operated as a needed checkdown option for Caleb Williams today. Swift is a borderline RB1/2 against the Jaguars next week. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Saquon Barkley is questionable to return in Week 12 against the Cowboys with a stinger.
items.text: Barkley has struggled with just seven yards on five attempts, and was seen grimacing on the sideline before exiting the contest. With Barkley unavailable, Will Shipley will likely see the majority of touches. - Christopher Crawford
